We can prove an interval during which no collision is possible. This is a guarantee about a finite mathematical system, with a checker that others can reuse.

A root-tracking program can restrict its search to a duration below the certified lower bound, leaving a margin. The exact roots cannot collide there. This does not bound Euler error, Newton convergence, or floating-point error. Degree two has its own exact pair formula. An arbitrary coefficient motion, or rounded measurements treated as exact roots, is a different problem.

The Riemann entire function has a heat deformation called H sub t, with the same heat sign. Its zeros are all real exactly when t is at least a threshold, Lambda. RH is equivalent to Lambda being at most zero. Rodgers and Tao proved Lambda is at least zero. Thus RH is equivalent to Lambda equaling zero. Shared zero dynamics connect the questions.

Our certificate uses finitely many roots and a finite diameter. The Riemann flow has infinitely many zeros, so an extension needs rigorous control of distant zeros and convergence of their interactions. Assuming every zero is real at time zero would assume RH. A uniform real-root interval below zero would contradict the known lower bound on Lambda. The open task is control toward zero from a known-real regime.

Use the proof as a finite-system guarantee, the checker for exact rational examples, and the quartic to benchmark numerical or local approximations. The saved suite covers twenty-five root configurations and one hundred rational-time checks; those tests support the implementation. The general statement comes from the proof. Novelty remains unestablished, and no transfer to infinitely many Riemann zeros has been proved.
